In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the literature review has revealed the need for more research to be done in order to better understand the characteristics, history and health care issues and needs of older LGBT adults, and to improve health care services for these individuals and families.
there is an urgent need to develop and test interventions to improve the health and quality of life for older LGBT persons.
there is a paucity of research on the health and health care needs of LGBT adults, especially older adults.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
older LGBT adults are at increased risk of experiencing health disparities due to their minority status, which can result in poorer quality of life and higher rates of morbidity and mortality.
older LGBT adults have a history of marginalization, mistreatment, and invisibility that has contributed to their health disparities and the lack of attention given to their health care needs.

hospice and palliatric care organizations need to address issues that are unique to LGBT older adults and to do so in a manner that is sensitive to their history, health disparities, and legal concerns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LGBT persons are a vulnerable population that deserves to have their needs addressed in a culturally competent manner.
the health care delivery system, including hospice care, must be prepared to address the specific needs and issues of older LGBT adults.

hospice and palliatric care organizations should be aware that LGBT older adults have unique health and health care concerns, and that these organizations can and should be at the forefront of addressing the needs of this population by providing culturally sensitive and appropriate care.
